newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's CPI up 3.0 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's CPI up 3.0 percent in 1996.

text.p: Morocco's Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 3.0 percent in 1996 to 147.7 points from 143.4 the year before, Moroccan Statistics Directorate said on Tuesday.
Main rise was in housing costs up 7.8 percent to 146.3 points in 1996 from 135.8 in 1995, followed by leisure costs up 6.2 percent to 140.0 last year from 131.8 the year before.

Food prices rose slightly by 0.7 percent to 155 points from 153.9 in 1995 mainly because of the variation in products, up 17.6, 15 and 7.3 percent respectively for fresh fish, canned vegetables and meat.
Vegetables and fruits fell 9.5 and 20.5 percent, the Directorate added.

It attributed the rise of medical care costs -- up 4.8 percent to 131.1 points in 1996 from 125.1 the year before-- to rises in medicals and medicines costs which jumped up 5.5 and 5.4 percent respectively.
The base year for the index set at 100 points is 1989.
